blocks.title: Boot and scheduling
items: Boot order: firmware (BIOS/UEFI) > bootloader (GRUB2) > kernel + initramfs > systemd (PID 1) > target. Config in /etc/default/grub then `grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg` (RHEL) or `update-grub` (Debian).
Reset a forgotten root password (RHEL): at GRUB press `e`, add `rd.break` to the linux line, boot, `mount -o remount,rw /sysroot`, `chroot /sysroot`, `passwd`, `touch /.autorelabel`, exit twice.
cron: `crontab -e` (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week command); system jobs in /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d. `at now + 5 min` runs once. Anacron catches up on missed jobs.

sheets.blurb: Partitions, filesystems, fstab, swap, LVM, RAID.

blocks.title: Disks, filesystems and LVM
rows: Mount, unmount, mount everything in fstab
Persistent mount (device, mount point, type, options, dump, fsck order)
pvcreate /dev/sdb1  /  vgcreate vg0 /dev/sdb1  /  lvcreate -L 5G -n data vg0
LVM: physical volume, volume group, logical volume
Grow XFS (mounted, by path) / ext4 (by device)
LVM status; add a disk to a group

blocks.title: Storage facts
items: XFS (default on RHEL) can grow but not shrink; ext4 can both. Btrfs and ZFS add snapshots and checksums.
RAID: 0 striping (no redundancy), 1 mirror, 5 striping with parity (1 disk), 6 double parity (2 disks), 10 mirror of stripes.
Use UUIDs in /etc/fstab, then test with `mount -a` before rebooting. NFS: `mount -t nfs server:/export /mnt`; autofs mounts on demand.

sheets.title: SELinux and security
sheets.blurb: Contexts, booleans, ports, logs and hardening.

blocks.title: SELinux (RHEL)
rows: Mode now (Enforcing, Permissive, Disabled); persistent in /etc/selinux/config
Define the default context for a path
Allow a service on a non-standard port

blocks.text: When a service is denied but permissions and the firewall look right, think SELinux: check the file context (`ls -Z`), booleans and ports before turning it off. `touch /.autorelabel` and reboot relabels the whole filesystem.

blocks.title: Security and logs
items: Logs: /var/log/messages (RHEL) or /var/log/syslog (Debian), /var/log/secure or auth.log (logins), /var/log/audit/audit.log, `journalctl`. rsyslog or journald forward logs; logrotate rotates them.

SSH hardening in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: `PermitRootLogin no`, `PasswordAuthentication no`, `AllowUsers`, change the port only as a minor measure; `systemctl reload sshd`. Fail2ban blocks repeated failures.
Least privilege: sudo rules, file permissions, remove unused packages and services. Keep systems patched; verify packages with `rpm -V` or checksums (`sha256sum`).
Encryption: LUKS (`cryptsetup luksFormat`, `luksOpen`) for disks, GPG for files, TLS certificates with `openssl`.

while read -r line; do ...; done < file

Script name, arguments, all arguments, count, last exit status
